purpose: Connect a prior circumstance to its consequence.
keywords: talk about time sequence duration habits
give explain a reason cause result
It snowed last night. As a result, the roads are frozen.
The train broke down. For that reason, our arrival was delayed.
The factory closed. As a result, many people lost their jobs.
restrictions: In this connective use その refers to the preceding situation; purpose is a separate reading.
mistake: Keep the preceding cause clear so it is not mistaken for “for that purpose.”
